title: How do you test Korean IME input when typing drives a racing game?
author: additiony41
selftext:
I designed Typing Sprint for MicroQuack, my browser racing game, and used Codex to help implement it. The mechanic is simple: matching letters move the robot. The tricky part is deciding when a letter is actually finished.

With a Korean input method (IME), the last syllable can change while you type. The current implementation lets the earlier, stable part of the string move the robot while holding back the syllable that is still being composed. At composition end, it checks the full string. Interim input does not count as a miss.

For anyone who has used an AI coding assistant to build an input-heavy game: what real keyboard or device would you test first to catch a syllable getting scored twice or skipped?
